history.summary: The Ruru Bhairav shrine stands within the Kankalitala Shakti Peetha temple complex (seq 1192/2487) in Kankalitala, Birbhum. RELATIONSHIP: every Shakti Peetha has paired shrines for Shakti and Kalabhairava — at Kankalitala the Shakti is addressed as Devgarbha and the Bhairava as Ruru (per the Tantrachudamani, which lists Kankalitala as the 28th sati peeth; also listed in the Die Hard Indian/Shakti-peetha tables as Kankalitala — Bone — Devgarbha — Ruru). Visitor accounts describe the Ruru Bhairav temple as a distinct shrine alongside the sacred Kali Kund within the complex. So this CSV row is not a separate temple: it is the guardian-deity shrine of the Kankalitala Shakti Peetha, documented here as a distinct record per the batch brief. Coordinates are those of the Kankalitala temple complex itself, since geocoding the shrine name alone returned an unrelated Shiva temple in Mohammad Bazar (rejected). The representative image is of the Kankalitala complex, not a standalone photo of the Bhairav shrine — no verified standalone image of the Ruru Bhairav shrine was found.

name: Ruru Bhairav Shrine
town_description: Kankalitala is a small temple town in the Bolpur-Sriniketan block of Birbhum district, about 10 km north-east of Bolpur/Santiniketan — the Ruru Bhairav shrine is a sub-shrine of the Kankalitala Shakti Peetha complex here.

travel.railway: Bolpur-Santiniketan (nearest major station); Rampurhat Junction also cited
travel.road: Within the Kankalitala temple complex on the Bolpur–Labhpur road, ~10 km from Santiniketan
